description: Verify the Protocol Address Length field of DUT's emitted ARP Request equals IP_ADDR_LEN (4) — declares how many bytes each IP address slot in the packet carries (RFC 826 packet generation)
approach:
[Objective]
The protocol-address-length byte of an ARP Request tells parsers how many bytes the sender_ip and target_ip fields occupy. For IPv4 that is 4. This case provokes a DUT ARP Request and asserts the field value.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. (No cache seeding — DUT's cache for HOST-1-IP starts empty.)

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message
   ⇒ DUT unicast-Nacks back; cache miss forces an ARP Request.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request
      - opcode          == 1
      - sender_mac      == DUT iface MAC
      - target_ip       == HOST-1-IP
      - proto_addr_len  == 4 (IP_ADDR_LEN)   ← key check

[Pass condition]
The observed ARP Request's Protocol Address Length equals 4.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_proto_addr_len — ARP Request seen but Protocol Address Length was not 4 (IP field width mismatch)
• Fail_timeout — No ARP Request observed within the window

verdicts.Pass: ARP Request carried proto_addr_len=4 (IPv4 width) — normal
verdicts.Fail_proto_addr_len: ARP Request emitted but proto_addr_len was not 4 — IP field width mismatch
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT ARP Request observed within the window
